parts.title: Vol 11-Section 1
parts.passageHtml:
{[A.][102335]} {[The British grass interrupted brome was said to be extinct, just like the Dodo.][102336]} {[Called interrupted brome because of its gappy seed-head, this unprepossessing grass was found nowhere else in the world, Gardening experts from the Victorian era were first to record it.][102351]} {[In the early 20th century, it grew far and wide across southern England.][102381]} {[But it quickly vanished and by 1972 was nowhere to be found.][102395]} {[Even the seeds stored at the Cambridge University Botanic Garden as an insurance policy were dead, having been mistakenly kept at room temperature.][102408]} {[Fans of the grass were devastated.][102431]}

{[B.][102440]} {[However, reports of its decline were not entirely correct.][102451]} {[Interrupted brome has enjoyed a revival, one that’s not due to science.][102461]} {[Because of the work of one gardening enthusiast, interrupted brome is thriving as a pot plant.][102473]} {[The relaunching into the wild of Britain’s almost extinct plant has excited conservationists everywhere.][102489]}

{[C. Originally, Philip Smith didn’t know that he had the very unusual grass at his own home.][102506]} {[When he heard about the grass becoming extinct, he wanted to do something surprising.][102523]} {[He attended a meeting of the British Botanical Society in Manchester in 1979, and seized his opportunity.][102538]} {[He said that it was so disappointing to hear about the demise of the interrupted brome.][102555]} {[“What a pity we didn’t research it further!][102572]} {[” he added.][102580]} {[Then.][102585]} {[all of a sudden he displayed his pots with so called “extinct grass” lot all to see.][102587]}

{[D. Smith had kept the seeds from the last stronghold of the grass, Pamisford in 1963.][102606]} {[It was then when the grass stalled to disappear from the wild.][102623]} {[Smith cultivated the grass, year after year.][102636]} {[Ultimately, it was his curiosity in the plant that saved it, not scientific or technological projects.][102644]}

{[E. For now, the bromes future is guaranteed.][102662]} {[The seeds front Smith’s plants have beet, securely stored in the cutting edge facilities of Millennium Seed Bank at Wakehurst Place in Sussex.][102670]} {[And living plants thrive at the botanic gardens at Kew, Edinburgh and Cambridge.][102694]} {[This year, seeds are also saved at sites all across the country and the grass now nourishes at several public gardens too.][102708]}

{[F. The grass will now be reintroduced to the British countryside.][102733]} {[As a part of the Species Recovery Project, the organisation English Nature will re-introduce interrupted brome into the agricultural landscape, provided willing farmers are found.][102744]} {[Alas, the grass is neither beautiful not practical.][102769]} {[it is undoubtedly a weed, a weed that nobody cares for these days.][102778]} {[The brome wax probably never widespread enough to annoy farmers and today, no one would appreciate its productivity or nutritious qualities.][102787]} {[As a grass, it leaves a lot to be desired by agriculturalists.][102807]}

{[G. Smith’s research has attempted to answer the question of where the grass came from.][102820]} {[His research points to mutations from other weedy grasses as the most likely source.][102836]} {[So close is the relationship that interrupted brome was originally deemed to be a mere variety of soil brome by the great Victorian taxonomist Professor Hackel.][102851]} {[A botanist from the 19th century, Druce, had taken notes on the grass and convinced his peers that the grass deserved its own status as a species.][102877]} {[Despite Druce growing up in poverty and his self-taught profession, he became the leading botanist of his time.][102903]}

{[H. Where the grass came from may be clear, but the timing of its birth may be tougher to find out.][102924]} {[A clue lies in its penchant for growing as a weed in fields shared with a fodder crop, in particular nitrogen-fixing legumes such as sainfoin, lucerne or clover.][102945]} {[According to agricultural historian Joan Thirsk, the humble sainfoin and its company were first noticed in Britain in the early 17th century.][102970]} {[Seeds brought in from the Continent were sown in pastures to feed horses and other livestock.][102993]} {[However, back then, only a few enthusiastic gentlemen were willing to use the new crops for their prized horses.][103010]}

{[I.][103031]} {[Not before too long though, the need to feed the parliamentary armies in Scotland, England and behind was more pressing than ever.][103054]} {[farmers were forced to produce more bread, cheese and beer.][103077]} {[And by 1650 the legumes were increasingly introduced into arable rotations, to serve as green nature to boost grain yields.][103088]} {[A bestseller of its day, Nathaniel Fiennes’s Improved Sainfoin, published in 1671, helped to spread the word.][103109]} {[With the advent of sainfoin, clover and lucerne.][103126]} {[Britain’s very own rogue grass had suddenly riveted everyone's attention.][103135]}

{[J.][103150]} {[Although the credit for the discovery of interrupted brome goes to a Miss A. M. Barnard, who collected the first specimens at Odsey, Bedfordshire, in 1849, the grass had probably lurked undetected in the English countryside for at least a hundred years.][103194]} {[Smith thinks the plant- the world’s version of the Dodo probably evolved in the late 17th or early 18th century, once sainfoin became established.][103230]} {[Due mainly to the development of the motor car and subsequent decline of fodder crops for horses, the brome declined rapidly over the 20th century.][103254]} {[Today, sainfoin has almost disappeared from the countryside, though occasionally its colourful flowers are spotted in lowland nature reserves.][103280]} {[More recently artificial fertilizers have made legume rotations unnecessary.][103300]}

{[K. The close relationship with out-of-fashion crops spells trouble for those seeking to re-establish interrupted brome in today’s countryside.][103312]} {[Much like the once common arable weeds, such as the corncockle, its seeds cannot survive long in the soil.][103331]} {[Each spring, the brome relied on farmers to resow its seeds; in the days before weed killers and advanced seed sieves, an ample supply would have contaminated supplies of crop seed.][103351]} {[However fragile seeds are not the brome’s only problem: this species is also unwilling to release its seeds as they ripen.][103382]} {[According to Smith.][103404]} {[The grass will struggle to survive even in optimal conditions.][103408]} {[It would be very difficult to thrive amongst its more resilient competitors found in today’s improved agricultural landscape.][103419]}

{[L. theless, interrupted brome’s reluctance to thrive independently may have some benefits.][103440]} {[Any farmer willing to foster this unique contribution to the world’s flora can rest assured that the grass will never become an invasive pest.][103452]} {[Restoring interrupted brome to its rightful home could bring other benefits too, particularly if this strange species is granted recognition as a national treasure.][103477]} {[Thanks to British farmers, interrupted brome was given the chance to evolve in the first place.][103501]} {[Conservationists would like to see the grass grow once again in its natural habitat and perhaps, one day, seeing the grass become a badge of honour for a new generation of environmentally conscious farmers.][103518]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 8:

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1-8 on you answer sheet, write:

TRUE                 if the statement is true

FALSE                if the statement is false

NOT GIVEN      if the information is not given in the passage

questions.text: The name of interrupted brome came from the unprepossessing grass disappeared from places in the world for a period.
questions.explanationHtml:
FALSE
 
unprepossessing (adj): trông bình thường, kém thu hút
"The name of interrupted brome came from the unprepossessing grass that disappeared from places in the world for a period" --> Tên "interrupted brome" có nguồn gốc từ 1 loài cỏ trông bình thường, kém thu hút đã biến mất khỏi nhiều nơi trên thế giới trong 1 giai đoạn nào đó LÀ FALSE vì loại cỏ này được gọi là "interrupted brome" do nó có "gappy seed-head" - phần nhuỵ hoa bị "gappy" là tính từ của "gap" có nghiều khoảng trống chứ không phải là do nó bị "disappeared" - biến mất khỏi nhiều nơi

questions.text: Interrupted brome seeds cannot sprout because they were kept accidentally at unsuitable temperature.
questions.explanationHtml:
TRUE
 
sprout (v) nảy mầm
accidentally (adv) vô tình, tai nạn không mong muốn = mistakenly (adv) một cách nhầm lẫn
"Interrupted brome seeds cannot sprout because they were kept accidentally at unsuitable temperature" --> loại cỏ này không "sprout" - nảy mầm được vì vô tình được bảo quản ở nhiệt độ không phù hợp LÀ TRUE do thông tin trong bài đề cập loài cỏ này bị chết do bị nhầm lẫn bảo quản ở nhiệt độ phòng - "room temperature"

questions.text: Philip Smith works at University of Manchester.
questions.explanationHtml:
NOT GIVEN
 
attend (v) tham dự
"Philip Smith works at University of Manchester" --> Phillip làm việc tại đại học Manchester LÀ NOT GIVEN vì trong bài chỉ đề cập là Phillip tham dự cuộc họp của British Botanical Society - tạm dịch là Hiệp hội Thực Vật Anh Quốc CHỨ KHÔNG ĐỀ CẬP ĐẾN học vấn của Phillip

questions.text: Kew Botanic Gardens will operate English Nature.
questions.explanationHtml:
NOT GIVEN
Thrive (v) phát triển mạnh mẽ, vượt bậc
"Kew Botanic Gardens will operate English Nature" --> Vườn thảo mộc ở Kew (1 quận ở London, Anh) sẽ vận hành tổ chức English Nature (1 tổ chức được lập ra để đưa loài cỏ này vào thiên nhiên trở lại) LÀ NOT GIVEN vì trong bài chỉ đề cập là loài cỏ này đã "thrive" - phát triển mạnh mẽ ở Kew CHỨ KHÔNG ĐỀ CẬP VIỆC vườn thảo mộc Kew sẽ vận hành English Nature.

questions.text: Interrupted brome grew unwantedly at the sides of sainfoin.
questions.explanationHtml:
FALSE
the grass = interrupted brome
penchant (n) có thiên hướng thích điều gì đó
"Interrupted brome grew unwantedly at the sides of sainfoin" --> Loài cỏ "interrupted brome" mọc 1 cách không mong muốn bên cạnh "sainfoin" LÀ SAI vì trong bài đề cập rất rõ là loài cỏ này có thiên hướng thích mọc trong cách cách đồng của "legumes" - các cây họ Đậu, và trong đó có "sainfoin" - cây hồng đậu

questions.text: Legumes were used for feeding livestock and enriching the soil.
questions.explanationHtml:
TRUE
 
enrich (v) làm giàu, làm cho màu mỡ = boost (v) thúc đẩy tăng trưởng
"Legumes were used for feeding livestock and enriching the soil" --> Các cây họ Đậu được dùng để làm thức ăn cho gia súc và làm màu mỡ cho đất LÀ TRUE vì những loại hạt đậu mà được đem từ "Continent" dùng để trồng nuôi ngựa và các loại gia súc khác. Ngoài ra, năm 1650, các cây họ Đậu được dùng để "boost grain yields" - tăng trưởng vụ mùa cho ngũ cốc

questions.text: The spread of seeds of interrupted brome depends on the harvesting of the farmers.
questions.explanationHtml:
FALSE
rivet (v) thu hút sự chú ý
"The spread of seeds of interrupted brome depends on the harvesting of the farmers" - Sự lan rộng của hạt của loài cỏ "interrupted brome" phụ thuộc vào việc thu hoạch của người nông dân LÀ SAI vì loài cỏ này được chú ý đến do nó có thiên hướng mọc cạnh các cây họ Đậu - "legumes" mà thời đó rất được trọng dụng

questions.text: Only the weed killers can stop interrupted brome from becoming an invasive pest.
questions.explanationHtml:
FALSE
 
"Only the weed killers can stop interrupted brome from becoming an invasive pest" --> Chỉ có "weed killers" - thuốc diệt cỏ là chặn được loài cỏ "interrupted brome" khỏi việc trở thành một "invasive pest" - thực vật gây hại xâm lấn LÀ SAI vì loài cỏ này có 1 vấn đề nữa là khi nó chín "ripen", nó không chịu nhả hạt để được trồng tiếp, và loài cỏ này "struggle" - rất khó khăn xoay xở để tồn tại dùng ở trong điều kiện tối ưu - "optimal conditions"

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 9 - 13:

Look at the following opinions or deeds (Questions 9-13) and the list of people below. Match each opinion or deed with the correct person, A-F. 

Write the correct letter, A-F, in boxes 9-13 on your answer sheet.

A          A. M. Barnard
B          Philip Smith
C          George Claridge Druce
D          Joan Thirsk
E          Professor Hackel
F          Nathaniel Fiennes

questions.text: Identified interrupted brome as another species of brome
questions.explanationHtml:
E
Identify sth as sth (v) nhận dạng cái gì đó như là cái gì đó
Loài cỏ này (interrupted brome) được cho rằng là sự biến thể - "variety" của "soil brome" - chính là 1 loài "brome" khác bởi Giáo sư Hackel

questions.text: Convinced others about the status of interrupted brome in the botanic world.
questions.explanationHtml:
C

 

convince (v) thuyết phục

Nhà thực vật học Druce đã thuyết phục mọi người rằng loài cỏ này xứng đáng được xem là 1 loài riêng biệt trong thế giới thực vật

questions.text: Said that sainfoin was first found more than 300 years ago.
questions.explanationHtml:
D

 

Theo nhà nông nghiệp sử gia Joan Thrisk, "sainfoin" được tìm thấy phát hiện vào đầu thế kỉ 17, nghĩa là cách đây hơn 300 năm

questions.text: Helped farmers know that sainfoin is useful for enriching the soil.
questions.explanationHtml:
F

 

"sainfoin" (1 trong các legumes - cây họ Đậu) được dùng để làm màu mỡ cho đất và "sainfoin" bán chạy nhất là của Nanthaniel, ông này tạo ra 1 loại "sainfoin" đã được cường hoá, càng giúp "spread the word" - lan truyền những tin tức tốt đẹp về sự hữu ích của các cây họ Đậu.

questions.text: Collected the first sample of interrupted brome.
questions.explanationHtml:
A

 

Người đầu tiên tìm được mẫu vật của loài cỏ "interrupted brome" là 1 người phụ nữ tên M.A.Barnard, ở Bedfordshire vào năm 1849.
